Two agencies, two direction models, one hub lock (Newcastle Central) with doNotGroup, plus a third and structurally distinct case at Sunderland (genuine shared-platform through-running, NOT a doNotGroup case) — see direction-model-memo.md and hazard-pack.md H1/H2/H6.

Metro modes v1: light rail only. Two lines: Yellow (St James-South Shields, 41 stations per report) and Green (Airport-South Hylton via Sunderland, 31 stations per report). This pack does not enumerate all stations on either line — only the named termini/via-points/hub/junction stations from the report. See coverageGaps.

Metro real-time: SCHEDULE-ONLY v1, no confirmed public feed found. This is a genuine 'no feed exists publicly' gap (unofficial app-only API at metro-rti.nexus.org.uk not usable), distinct in kind from the National Rail account block below.

National Rail modes v1: heavy rail, destination-board model (not line+terminus). BLOCKED pending DARWIN_LDB_TOKEN — see coverageGaps. Build the catalog/adapter normally per Nico's report; do not wire the token until it exists.

Hub lock: Newcastle Central (NCL CRS). Metro Central is a deep-tube station directly below the National Rail main-line platforms. doNotGroup Metro vs National Rail at this station — separate infrastructure, separate operators, separate boarding areas, no walk-through connection named in the report.

Sunderland is NOT modeled as a hub-lock/doNotGroup pair like Newcastle Central. The report states Metro Green Line and Northern Trains use the SAME platforms on the SAME track between Pelaw and Sunderland (genuine shared-platform case). Modeled as sunderlandSharedPlatform below: a single shared-platform through-running station, board must mix both services (once National Rail is unblocked) rather than split by mode tab. See direction-model-memo.md for full reasoning, including a flagged inconsistency with how South Yorkshire's already-merged pack actually described the Rotherham Central precedent Nico cited (Rotherham Central's own pack states no shared platform there, contradicting this report's characterization of it as a comparable case — flagged, not resolved, in hazard-pack.md H1).

Pelaw is a Metro-only junction, not a separate National Rail station and not a doNotGroup case. South of Pelaw is Green-exclusive track to South Hylton; north of Pelaw the Green Line's track becomes shared with National Rail toward Sunderland. Whether Yellow Line services call at Pelaw itself is not stated in the report — flagged as a gap, not guessed either way.

Berwick-upon-Tweed (BWK) is National Rail only, England's northernmost East Coast Main Line station, Scotland boundary. Included in this pack's National Rail boundary list per the report's own station table, but whether additional ECML stations between Newcastle and Berwick (e.g. Morpeth, Alnmouth) belong to North East's catalog is NOT stated in the report — real gap, not enumerated here, do not guess additional intermediate ECML stations.

Darlington (DRL) is EXCLUDED from this pack. The report flags it as a boundary candidate needing clarification against East Midlands, but East Midlands' own oracle report and published pack do not mention Darlington at all (checked: no match across docs/east-midlands-d1/*.md, *.json). The boundary is genuinely unresolved on both sides — flagged in hazard-pack.md, not assigned by guess.

City lands as 'Coming Soon' (status stays planned; there is no separate coming-soon enum value in registry.js) until National Rail is unblocked AND a confirmed Metro real-time source is found (or the region ships Metro schedule-only-permanently, a decision for Tim/Jim, not this pack), same overall status shape as West Midlands / Greater Manchester / Liverpool City Region / East Midlands / South Yorkshire.

Metro line station arrays below are TERMINI + NAMED VIA-POINTS + hub/junction stations only, as given by the report's line descriptions and station table — NOT a full ordered intermediate stop list (41 + 31 stations total per the report, only a subset named). This is a real gap; see coverageGaps and hazard-pack.md H3/H4/H5.

gtfsRouteIdsIfKnown is left empty for both Metro lines — GTFS static feed is confirmed to exist (f-bus~dft~gov~uk) but this pack does not pull it to extract route_ids; that's a D2 task for Jim, not invented here.

printedInnerCityNames.note: Two locks sharing one printed name, deep-tube Metro box below main rail platforms, no walk-through connection named. doNotGroup between them. See hazard-pack.md H1/H6. Sunderland is a separate, non-hub-lock case — see sunderlandSharedPlatform below, do not conflate with the Newcastle Central doNotGroup pattern.

coverageGaps: Metro real-time: NO confirmed public feed found. This is a genuine 'no source exists publicly' gap, not the standard account-registration block — unofficial app-only API at metro-rti.nexus.org.uk not usable as a machine-readable source. Confirm with Nexus/DB Regio whether GTFS-RT or a documented API will be published before this can move past schedule-only v1.

National Rail real-time: OpenLDBWS documented and technically live, but BLOCKED at the account level (AU-registered RDM account; Tim re-registering with UK address). Not a feed problem. Do not wire DARWIN_LDB_TOKEN until it exists. Same blocker as East Midlands / West Midlands / Greater Manchester / Liverpool City Region / South Yorkshire — already accepted, not re-flagged as a new blocker.

National Rail licensing: OGL 2.0 baseline permits redistribution with attribution, but the RDM Platform Agreement's language on downstream redistribution to third-party rider clients is UNCLEAR in public sources. Confidence: unclear (per oracle report License section). OPEN ITEM FOR TIM ONLY — do not resolve here; same open item already raised for East Midlands and South Yorkshire.

Metro's two lines' full intermediate stop order (41 + 31 stations) is not in the oracle report — only named termini/via-points/hub/junction stations. Do not treat the 'stations' arrays below as complete; pull a confirmed GTFS feed (f-bus~dft~gov~uk) for the real ordered list at D2.
Whether Yellow Line calls at Pelaw itself (vs. only the shared South Gosforth-Pelaw corridor) is not stated in the report — flagged in direction-model-memo.md, not resolved here.

National Rail has no printed route/line map to transcribe (Darwin is a real-time per-station board product) — no 'lines' array is provided for National Rail in this pack, only the hub, the Sunderland shared-platform case, and the boundary station list. See direction-model-memo.md for the destination+operator model recommended instead of line+terminus.

Berwick-upon-Tweed's northern boundary against a future Rest-of-Scotland pack (no such pack exists yet) is unresolved, including whether intermediate ECML stations (Morpeth, Alnmouth) belong to North East's catalog — not enumerated, not guessed.
Darlington boundary against East Midlands is unresolved on both sides (East Midlands' pack does not claim it either) — excluded from this pack's station list entirely pending clarification.

A cross-region inconsistency is flagged, not resolved: this report describes Rotherham Central (South Yorkshire) as a same-platform precedent for Sunderland, but South Yorkshire's own already-merged pack states Rotherham Central has no shared platform with National Rail. See hazard-pack.md H1 for detail. Whoever owns UK station-graph QA should reconcile which description is accurate; this pack builds Sunderland only from what this report says about Sunderland itself.
No buses, no other rail modes, no Metro real-time in v1 scope, per the oracle report.
